page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU supports a clock frequency up to 4.5 GHz, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic accelerations such as AES and SHA-NI.

The configuration provides 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Attached local storage consists of a 945 GB NVMe solid-state drive, offering high-throughput local scratch space alongside Azure Premium Storage capability. The server contains no discrete hardware GPUs, relying solely on processor-based execution.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core execution speed, with top-tier rankings in stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core evaluation. Multi-core performance metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench align with midrange peer averages for 16-vCPU instances. In light model inference, the instance delivers top-tier throughput for 135M parameter models, but execution slows considerably when scaling to medium and large parameter models due to the absence of dedicated accelerators and memory bandwidth constraints.

With its combination of strong single-threaded compute, 945 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe storage, and balanced system memory, the D16ads_v7 offers balanced resource efficiency for workloads requiring low latency per thread. Primary workload targets include relational databases, Redis cache nodes, web and application serving, continuous integration builds, and data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64.0 GB of RAM, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It features a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD and supports AVX-512 instruction sets, but omits discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark data reflects top-tier single-core performance across Geekbench and compression utilities, while multi-core metrics and memory bandwidth land within expected mid-tier distributions. CPU-bound small-model inference executes efficiently, though throughput declines rapidly on larger language models. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with strong single-threaded processing makes this instance well-suited for relational database engines, caching tiers, compilation tasks, and general enterprise application hosting.
